doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Origin of the Levy name on a Plaquemines Parish plantation
summary: The name came from his paternal grandfather's enslaved family owned by French Jews in Plaquemines Parish.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And Levy – what’s the history of that name?

Levy, as far as I could discern – the periods that I traced it was through my father’s father, who was part of a slave thing. All of the people on the plantation had the name of Levy. In other words, all of the slaves had the name of Levy. So that’s where the name came from.
Was this in New Orleans? In Louisiana?

This was in – it was outside of New Orleans. The plantation that these slaves worked on was called Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana. There was the slave owner – which a lot of time people said that the Jewish people never had any slaves, but these were Jewish – French Jews, and they did have slaves. This was from that slavery – from that plantation that the name Levy derived and followed through with my self . . .
Do you know what type of plantation it was? What was grown? What was on the plantation?
No. I don’t know what was grown on it, on a plantation.
